title: GPU memory portfolio budgeting for KV, weights, and activation headroom
creator: Aisha Tan
description: Introduce a portfolio-style GPU memory budgeting strategy that treats weights, KV cache, and activations as allocation classes with configurable shares and explicit headroom to reduce OOMs while optimizing utilization and cost for continuous-batching workloads.
background: We currently apply ad-hoc soft watermarks and eviction heuristics for KV cache and activations. That approach reduces some OOMs but leaves substantial stranded memory (reserved for weights or bursts) and inconsistent tail latencies during mixed workloads. Operators lack a single source-of-truth model for expected headroom by tenant and machine class. This ticket defines a repeatable, measurable budgeting system that can be simulated and deployed incrementally.
proposal: Define three primary memory buckets: weights_reserve, kv_reserve, activation_buffer.
Introduce a configurable safety_margin (headroom) expressed in absolute MB and as a percentile of observed spike distribution (e.g., 99th).

Compute per-instance portfolio shares using historical telemetry: share_weights = median(weight_bytes / gpu_total_free), share_kv = p80(kv_bytes / gpu_total_free), share_activations = p95(activation_peak / gpu_total_free). Normalize so shares + safety_margin <= 1.

Implement a budgeting engine that: (a) reads current foot-print telemetry, (b) reconciles target reserves vs real-time usage, (c) exposes a periodic rebalancer that slides allocations on low-risk windows, and (d) triggers emergency eviction when activation_buffer usage exceeds temporary soft limit.

Expose policy knobs: conservative/aggressive modes, tenant-priority multipliers, burst_credit buckets for short-lived surges, and a configurable eviction order (activation -> kv -> weight-swap-preempt).
Simulation harness: extend existing memory-sim (scripts/mem-sim) to run replayed traces with the portfolio allocator and measure OOM rate, tail latency, and stranded_memory fraction.
Rollout phasing: start with a canary fleet, observe metrics for two weeks, then widen to mixed-tenant pools before cluster-wide adoption.
tradeoffs: Tighter kv_reserve reduces OOMs from evicting weights, but increases activation OOM risk under heavy burst patterns.
Large safety_margin improves reliability at cost of utilization; percentage-based margins can adapt but may underprotect for long-tail spikes.
Reactive eviction introduces jitter; preemptive reservation reduces jitter but can leave memory idle during steady-state.
Complex budgeting increases scheduler complexity and rollout risk; will require strong observability and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation results show >= 30% reduction in OOM events for mixed continuous-batching traces compared to baseline heuristics.
Tail-99 latency for gen requests does not regress by more than 5% on canary fleet under representative load.
Dashboard cards for per-instance reserves (weights/kv/activations/headroom) are available in Console and populated for canary cluster.
Runbook updated with emergency eviction steps, and SRE signoff obtained.
A migration plan for pinned workloads (where weights_store is immutable) exists and is validated with a dry-run.
tasks: Design memory portfolio schema and config proto (ENG + Runtime API)
Add telemetry aggregation keys for per-request activation_peak and kv_deltas
Implement portfolio allocator in runtime: reserve accounting + periodic rebalancer
Build simulation harness and run replay tests across three representative traces
Create Console dashboards and alert rules for reserve saturation and stranded_memory
Canary deploy to gpu-pool-canary, run 14-day observation
Iterate on policies (burst_credit, priority multipliers) after canary feedback
Author runbook and obtain SRE/Infra approval for global rollout
telemetry_queries: OOM signal: count_over_time(oom_events[1d]) grouped by host_type
Burst_credit consumption: sum(burst_credit_used) by tenant over 24h
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design): finalize schema and low-level API (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (Sim): run replay simulation across historical traces; tune default shares (3 weeks)
Phase 2 (Canary): enable on gpu-pool-canary (10% capacity) with read-only mode for 48h, then enforcement mode for 14 days
Phase 3 (Expand): expand to mixed-tenant pools with telemetry gating and capacity guardrails (4 weeks)
Phase 4 (GA): cluster-wide roll with migration scripts and opt-out knobs for critical tenants
reviews: 2026-01-12: PM review (Sana Kapoor) - asked for customer impact analysis and suggested adding per-tenant quotas in docs.
2026-01-20: SRE review (Danielle White) - requested canary duration be at least 14 days and alert thresholds for headroom violation to be conservative by default.
2026-02-05: Infra review (Luca Moretti) - recommended precomputing share coefficients in control-plane to avoid runtime CPU spikes; flagged potential serialization cost.
2026-02-18: Security review requested (pending) - required confirmation that telemetry identifiers contain no PII.
notes: Implementation will avoid immediate eviction of weights except in defined preemption windows; instead weights are candidates for graceful offload to remote storage based on model hotness metrics.
We will instrument an inexpensive fallback: if portfolio allocator fails to compute an allocation (rare), runtime will fall back to current soft-watermark heuristic and emit an alert.
Expect multiple tuning passes: default conservative parameters for GA, and an aggressive profile for premium tenants that buy lower-cost headroom via reserved capacity contracts.
